The award was conferred on the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) in recognition of its efforts to strengthen accountability in personal data processing, promote regulatory transparency and advance data protection governance.
The recognition places Nigeria among jurisdictions gaining international attention for their approaches to privacy regulation, particularly as the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence, digital financial services and other emerging technologies increases concerns over the collection, processing and security of personal information.
The commemorative citation accompanying the award acknowledged the Commission’s exemplary governance, transparency, compliance frameworks and leadership commitment to privacy and data protection.
Speaking on the achievement, the National Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer of the NDPC, Dr Vincent Olatunji, described accountability as fundamental to effective data protection and essential to building public confidence in Nigeria’s expanding digital economy.
According to him, “Excellence in Accountability is the hallmark of data protection. It is a principle that data controllers and data processors must uphold in order to earn the trust of over 230 million data subjects in Nigeria and position the country as a destination of choice for investors.”
Olatunji said the recognition reflected the Federal Government’s commitment to building a trusted and sustainable digital ecosystem, adding that the achievement was particularly significant given that it came less than four years after President Bola Tinubu signed the Nigeria Data Protection Act into law.
Beyond winning the accountability category, Nigeria was also named a finalist in two other competitive categories: Education and Public Awareness, and Innovation, highlighting the country’s efforts to strengthen data protection through public sensitisation, regulatory oversight and innovative compliance mechanisms.
A major feature of Nigeria’s regulatory framework is its public-private partnership approach, through which the Commission has licensed 367 Data Protection Compliance Organisations (DPCOs) to provide compliance services to businesses and institutions across the country.
The arrangement is designed to extend the Commission’s regulatory reach, strengthen compliance monitoring and promote accountability among more than 500,000 data controllers and processors of major importance operating in Nigeria.
The model has also attracted interest from foreign data protection authorities, which are studying its potential application in expanding regulatory capacity and encouraging private-sector participation in data protection enforcement.
The Global Privacy Assembly is a leading international forum bringing together data protection and privacy authorities from more than 145 jurisdictions worldwide. Its 48th annual conference provided an opportunity for regulators to discuss emerging privacy challenges, strengthen cross-border cooperation and develop common approaches to protecting personal information.
The assembly’s broader discussions this year also focused on emerging challenges associated with artificial intelligence, privacy-enhancing technologies, children’s data protection and digital governance.
Nigeria’s recognition comes amid growing concerns over data breaches, identity theft, unauthorised access to personal information and the increasing use of digital platforms to process sensitive consumer data.
With financial institutions, telecommunications companies, technology firms and public institutions handling increasing volumes of Nigerians’ personal information, effective enforcement of data protection regulations remains critical to building confidence in the country’s digital economy.
The award is therefore expected to boost Nigeria’s visibility in international privacy governance, although sustained enforcement, public awareness, and accountability among organisations handling personal information will remain key measures of the country’s progress.
